Module.title: Walk-Around Check
Module.subtitle: Visual Inspection
Module.description: Inspect a Class V (LPG) forklift before use: forks, mast, chains, hydraulic hoses, tires, counterweight, LPG tank/battery, seat belt, overhead guard, and ground leaks, then confirm dashboard indicators, steering, brakes, lift/tilt, travel, and warning devices.

Module.title: Load Handling and Operational Controls
Module.subtitle: Operational Controls
Module.description: Practice basic forklift operational controls in a simplified guided drive: engine start-up, acceleration, braking, and steering, without real vehicle physics or collision.

Module.subtitle: Getting Started

Module.title: Post-Operation and Secure Parking
Module.subtitle: Secure Parking
Module.description: Park the forklift inside a painted bay on a cone-lined route, then secure it: fork lowering, neutral controls, brake engagement, power off, and reporting. Hitting a cone fails the parking attempt.

Module.title: Pallet Handling Assessment
Module.subtitle: Load Safety
Module.description: Apply load-handling judgment under fail conditions: respect rated capacity, avoid traffic cones, and brake smoothly so the load stays on the forks. Overloading, collisions, and sudden stops fail the attempt.

Hotspot.label: Forks
Hotspot.title: Forks
Hotspot.subtitle: Load Handling Parts
Hotspot.description:
Support and lift pallets or loads when correctly inserted and spaced.

**What to inspect**

Check fork tips, heel area, visible cracks, and locking pins before use.

**Safety**

Never stand under raised forks, and keep the load centered before lifting.

**Quick checklist**

- Check fork tips
- Confirm locking pins
- Keep load centered

*Related training: Load Handling and Operational Controls*
Hotspot.functionText: Support and lift pallets or loads when correctly inserted and spaced.
Hotspot.inspectionReminder: Check fork tips, heel area, visible cracks, and locking pins before use.
Hotspot.safetyNote: Never stand under raised forks, and keep the load centered before lifting.
Hotspot.inspect: Check fork tips, heel area, and mounting pins for cracks, bending, or wear.
Hotspot.safeFeedback: Forks show no visible cracks, bending, or wear in this state.
Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: Damaged or bent forks can fail under load and must be reported before use.

Hotspot.label: Mast
Hotspot.title: Mast
Hotspot.subtitle: Load Handling Parts
Hotspot.description:
Guides the vertical movement of the carriage and forks.

**What to inspect**

Look for visible damage, obstruction, or unsafe movement in the lift path.

**Safety**

Keep hands, feet, and loose clothing away from the mast and lift chain path.

**Quick checklist**

- Look for visible damage
- Check lift path clearance
- Raise load smoothly

*Related training: Walk-Around Check*
Hotspot.functionText: Guides the vertical movement of the carriage and forks.
Hotspot.inspectionReminder: Look for visible damage, obstruction, or unsafe movement in the lift path.
Hotspot.safetyNote: Keep hands, feet, and loose clothing away from the mast and lift chain path.
Hotspot.inspect: Inspect the mast channels and lift path for cracks, bending, or obstruction.
Hotspot.safeFeedback: No mast crack or damage is visible in this state.
Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: Mast crack detected. Lifting operation is unsafe.

Hotspot.label: Lift Chain
Hotspot.title: Lift Chain
Hotspot.subtitle: Load Handling Parts
Hotspot.description:
Transfers lifting force through the mast assembly.

**What to inspect**

Observe for slack, uneven movement, or visible damage before operation.

**Safety**

Do not touch or inspect the chain while the engine is running or the forks are moving.

**Quick checklist**

- Look for slack
- Check for uneven movement
- Keep clear while lifting

*Related training: Walk-Around Check*
Hotspot.functionText: Transfers lifting force through the mast assembly.
Hotspot.inspectionReminder: Observe for slack, uneven movement, or visible damage before operation.
Hotspot.safetyNote: Do not touch or inspect the chain while the engine is running or the forks are moving.
Hotspot.inspect: Check the lift chains for proper lubrication and any broken, stretched, or damaged links.
Hotspot.safeFeedback: Lift chains appear properly lubricated with no visible damage.
Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: Damaged, dry, or stretched chains must be reported before lifting operations.

Hotspot.label: Carriage
Hotspot.title: Carriage
Hotspot.subtitle: Load Handling Parts
Hotspot.description:
Holds the forks and moves along the mast during lifting and lowering.

**What to inspect**

Check fork attachment points and confirm there is no visible damage.

**Safety**

Confirm the carriage is stable before handling any load.

**Quick checklist**

- Check fork attachment
- Check visible cracks
- Confirm smooth travel

*Related training: Load Handling and Operational Controls*
Hotspot.functionText: Holds the forks and moves along the mast during lifting and lowering.
Hotspot.inspectionReminder: Check fork attachment points and confirm there is no visible damage.
Hotspot.safetyNote: Confirm the carriage is stable before handling any load.

Hotspot.label: Operator Area
Hotspot.title: Operator Area
Hotspot.subtitle: Operator and Controls
Hotspot.description:
Contains the seat, steering, pedals, levers, and dashboard controls used by the operator.

**What to inspect**

Confirm controls are understood, accessible, and checked before operation.

**Safety**

Fasten the seat belt and confirm controls are understood before operation.

**Quick checklist**

- Fasten seat belt
- Check mirrors
- Test horn and brakes

*Related training: Walk-Around Check*
Hotspot.functionText: Contains the seat, steering, pedals, levers, and dashboard controls used by the operator.
Hotspot.inspectionReminder: Confirm controls are understood, accessible, and checked before operation.
Hotspot.safetyNote: Fasten the seat belt and confirm controls are understood before operation.

Hotspot.label: Overhead Guard
Hotspot.title: Overhead Guard
Hotspot.subtitle: Stability and Structure
Hotspot.description:
Helps protect the operator from falling objects within the forklift safety limits.

**What to inspect**

Check for visible bending, cracks, or missing sections.

**Safety**

Do not operate if the overhead guard is visibly damaged.

**Quick checklist**

- Check structural damage
- Keep guard unobstructed
- Never remove the guard

*Related training: Walk-Around Check*
Hotspot.functionText: Helps protect the operator from falling objects within the forklift safety limits.
Hotspot.inspectionReminder: Check for visible bending, cracks, or missing sections.
Hotspot.safetyNote: Do not operate if the overhead guard is visibly damaged.
Hotspot.inspect: Check the overhead guard for bending, cracks, or missing sections.
Hotspot.safeFeedback: The overhead guard shows no visible structural damage in this state.
Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: Loose or missing bolt detected on the overhead guard. Report before operation.

Hotspot.label: Counterweight
Hotspot.title: Counterweight
Hotspot.subtitle: Stability and Structure
Hotspot.description:
Balances the forklift against the weight of the load.

**What to inspect**

Confirm rear clearance and observe rear swing when maneuvering.

**Safety**

Watch rear swing and never exceed the rated load capacity.

**Quick checklist**

- Avoid overloading
- Watch rear swing
- Respect capacity plate

*Related training: Load Handling and Operational Controls*
Hotspot.functionText: Balances the forklift against the weight of the load.
Hotspot.inspectionReminder: Confirm rear clearance and observe rear swing when maneuvering.
Hotspot.safetyNote: Watch rear swing and never exceed the rated load capacity.
Hotspot.inspect: Check the counterweight mounting and rear clearance for visible damage.
Hotspot.safeFeedback: Counterweight mounting appears secure in this state.
Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: A loose or damaged counterweight affects forklift balance.

Hotspot.label: Tires
Hotspot.title: Tires
Hotspot.subtitle: Stability and Structure
Hotspot.description:
Support forklift movement and stability across the work surface.

**What to inspect**

Check for visible wear, damage, or unsafe tire condition.

**Safety**

Damaged or underinflated tires can affect stability and steering.

**Quick checklist**

- Check visible wear
- Check inflation or damage
- Report unsafe tire condition

*Related training: Walk-Around Check*
Hotspot.functionText: Support forklift movement and stability across the work surface.
Hotspot.inspectionReminder: Check for visible wear, damage, or unsafe tire condition.
Hotspot.safetyNote: Damaged or underinflated tires can affect stability and steering.
Hotspot.inspect: Check tire condition, wheel nuts, and tire pressure (for pneumatic tires).
Hotspot.safeFeedback: Tires and wheel nuts appear acceptable in this state.
Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: Unsafe tire condition affects steering and stability.

Hotspot.label: Capacity Plate
Hotspot.title: Capacity Plate
Hotspot.subtitle: Safety and Identification
Hotspot.description:
Shows rated load capacity and important forklift specifications.

**What to inspect**

Read the rated capacity and load center before handling loads.

**Safety**

Do not lift a load beyond the capacity shown on the plate.

**Quick checklist**

- Read rated capacity
- Confirm load center
- Follow plate limits

*Related training: Load Handling and Operational Controls*
Hotspot.functionText: Shows rated load capacity and important forklift specifications.
Hotspot.inspectionReminder: Read the rated capacity and load center before handling loads.
Hotspot.safetyNote: Do not lift a load beyond the capacity shown on the plate.

Hotspot.label: Warning Devices
Hotspot.title: Warning Devices
Hotspot.subtitle: Safety and Identification
Hotspot.description:
Includes lights, horn, and backup alarm used to alert nearby workers.

**What to inspect**

Test horn, lights, beacon, and backup alarm during pre-operation checks.

**Safety**

Do not operate if required warning devices are not working.

**Quick checklist**

- Test horn
- Check lights
- Check backup alarm

*Related training: Walk-Around Check*
Hotspot.functionText: Includes lights, horn, and backup alarm used to alert nearby workers.
Hotspot.inspectionReminder: Test horn, lights, beacon, and backup alarm during pre-operation checks.
Hotspot.safetyNote: Do not operate if required warning devices are not working.

Hotspot.label: Hydraulic Hoses
Hotspot.title: Hydraulic Hoses
Hotspot.subtitle: Hydraulic hoses and cylinders
Hotspot.description:
Check hydraulic hoses and cylinders for visible leaks, cracks, or wear.

**Why it matters**

Hydraulic leaks can affect lifting safety and must be reported before operation.
Hotspot.inspect: Check hydraulic hoses and cylinders for visible leaks, cracks, or wear.
Hotspot.safeFeedback: No hydraulic leak is visible in this state.
Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: Hydraulic leak detected. Forklift should not be used.

Hotspot.label: LPG Tank and Battery
Hotspot.title: LPG Tank and Battery
Hotspot.subtitle: LPG tank, mounting bracket, and battery area
Hotspot.description:
Check the propane tank, mounting bracket, hose fittings, and battery area for leaks, damage, or corrosion.

**Why it matters**

A propane leak or unsafe battery condition is hazardous and must be reported before operation.
Hotspot.inspect: Check the propane tank, mounting bracket, hose fittings, and battery area for leaks, damage, or corrosion.
Hotspot.safeFeedback: No LPG leak, damaged mounting, or battery concern is visible in this state.
Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: A propane leak or unsafe battery condition is hazardous. Report before operation.

Hotspot.label: Seat Belt
Hotspot.title: Seat Belt
Hotspot.subtitle: Operator seat and restraint
Hotspot.description:
Check the seat condition and confirm the seat belt latches and retracts properly.

**Why it matters**

A damaged or non-functioning seat belt must be reported before operation.
Hotspot.inspect: Check the seat condition and confirm the seat belt latches and retracts properly.
Hotspot.safeFeedback: Seat and seat belt appear in working condition in this state.
Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: A damaged or non-functioning seat belt must be reported before operation.

Hotspot.label: Ground Leaks
Hotspot.title: Ground Leaks
Hotspot.subtitle: Ground beneath the forklift
Hotspot.description:
Check the ground beneath the forklift for oil, fuel, hydraulic fluid, or coolant leaks.

**Why it matters**

Any fluid leak on the ground must be reported before operation.
Hotspot.inspect: Check the ground beneath the forklift for oil, fuel, hydraulic fluid, or coolant leaks.
Hotspot.safeFeedback: No fluid leak is visible on the ground in this state.
Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: Fluid leak detected on the ground. Forklift is unsafe for operation.

Hotspot.label: Ignition Switch
Hotspot.title: Ignition Switch
Hotspot.subtitle: Engine start
Hotspot.description:
Turn the key to start the engine before beginning the operational checks.

**Why it matters**

The engine must be running before operational checks can be made.
Hotspot.inspect: Turn the key to start the engine before beginning the operational checks.
Hotspot.safeFeedback: Engine started. Continue with the engine-on checks.
Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: The engine must be running before operational checks can be made.

Hotspot.label: Dashboard
Hotspot.title: Dashboard
Hotspot.subtitle: Dashboard indicators
Hotspot.description:
Read the dashboard gauges and decide whether each reading is normal.

**Why it matters**

A dashboard warning must be reported before operation.
Hotspot.inspect: Read the dashboard gauges and decide whether each reading is normal.
Hotspot.safeFeedback: Dashboard gauges are ready to be read.
Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: A dashboard warning must be reported before operation.

Hotspot.label: Horn
Hotspot.title: Horn
Hotspot.subtitle: Safety devices
Hotspot.description:
Press the horn and confirm an audible warning sounds.

**Why it matters**

A horn that does not sound must be reported.
Hotspot.inspect: Press the horn and confirm an audible warning sounds.
Hotspot.safeFeedback: Horn responds. Audible warning device is working.
Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: A horn that does not sound must be reported.

Hotspot.label: Headlights
Hotspot.title: Headlights
Hotspot.subtitle: Safety devices
Hotspot.description:
Switch on the headlights and confirm both lamps light up.

**Why it matters**

A headlight that does not light must be reported.
Hotspot.inspect: Switch on the headlights and confirm both lamps light up.
Hotspot.safeFeedback: Headlights respond. Lighting check passes.
Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: A headlight that does not light must be reported.

Hotspot.label: Tail Lights
Hotspot.title: Tail Lights
Hotspot.subtitle: Safety devices

Confirm the tail lights light up at the rear of the forklift.

**Why it matters**

A tail light that does not light must be reported.
Hotspot.inspect: Confirm the tail lights light up at the rear of the forklift.
Hotspot.safeFeedback: Tail lights respond. Lighting check passes.
Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: A tail light that does not light must be reported.

Hotspot.label: Turn Signals

Hotspot.label: Warning Beacon
Hotspot.title: Warning Beacon
Hotspot.subtitle: Safety devices
Hotspot.description:
Confirm the warning beacon flashes so nearby workers can see the forklift.

A beacon that does not flash must be reported.
Hotspot.inspect: Confirm the warning beacon flashes so nearby workers can see the forklift.
Hotspot.safeFeedback: Warning beacon responds. Visual warning check passes.
Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: A beacon that does not flash must be reported.

Hotspot.label: Backup Alarm
Hotspot.title: Backup Alarm
Hotspot.subtitle: Safety devices

Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: A silent backup alarm must be reported.

Hotspot.label: Steering Response
Hotspot.title: Steering Response
Hotspot.subtitle: Operational controls
Hotspot.description:
Turn the steering wheel and check for smooth response with no excessive play.

Excessive steering play must be reported before operation.
Hotspot.inspect: Turn the steering wheel and check for smooth response with no excessive play.
Hotspot.safeFeedback: Steering responds smoothly with no excessive play.
Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: Excessive steering play must be reported before operation.

Hotspot.label: Brakes

Test the service brake and the parking brake for correct response.

**Why it matters**

A brake that does not hold must be reported immediately.
Hotspot.inspect: Test the service brake and the parking brake for correct response.
Hotspot.safeFeedback: Service brake and parking brake respond correctly.
Hotspot.unsafeFeedback: A brake that does not hold must be reported immediately.

Hotspot.title: Lift and Tilt Functions
Hotspot.subtitle: Operational controls
Hotspot.description:
Raise, lower, and tilt the mast and listen for unusual noise.

Hotspot.inspect: Raise, lower, and tilt the mast and listen for unusual noise.
Hotspot.safeFeedback: Mast raises, lowers, and tilts smoothly with no unusual noise.

Hotspot.subtitle: Operational controls

Course.title: Scenario Briefing
Course.objective: Prepare for a simplified guided driving exercise, without real forklift physics.
Course.instructions: Review why operational-control familiarization comes before supervised practical training.
Course.hint: The goal is control familiarization and decision-making, not physics-accurate driving.

content.body:
This simplified simulation lets you practice the basic operating controls of a forklift: starting the engine, accelerating, braking, and steering.

This is a simplified control-familiarization exercise, not a physics-accurate driving simulator. It does not model collisions, real vehicle dynamics, or unsupervised operation.

Each guided step introduces one control at a time before combining them in a short driving course.
objectives: Identify the basic operating controls used to start and drive a forklift in this simulation.
Practice accelerating and braking smoothly to control forklift speed.
Practice steering left and right while maintaining a safe course.
Combine starting, accelerating, braking, and steering in a short guided driving course.

Course.title: Controls & Engine Start
Course.objective: Learn the WASD driving controls and start the engine.
Course.instructions: Press E to start the engine, then try W, A, S, and D at least once each on the open practice pad.
Course.hint: The engine must be running before the forklift will accelerate or steer.

Course.title: Accelerate Course
Course.objective: Practice accelerating the forklift forward using the W key.
Course.instructions: Press E to start the engine if needed, then press W to accelerate forward to the finish line.
Course.hint: Hold W steadily - you do not need to reach maximum speed to finish.

checkpoints.label: Finish Line
checkpoints.completeMessage: You accelerated forward and crossed the finish line.

Course.title: Accelerate and Brake
Course.objective: Practice accelerating and braking to a controlled stop.
Course.instructions: Press W to accelerate, then press S in time to stop inside the marked stop zone.
Course.hint: Begin braking before you reach the zone - stopping distance is not instant.

checkpoints.label: Stop Zone
checkpoints.completeMessage: You braked in time and stopped inside the marked zone.

Course.title: Left and Right Turning
Course.objective: Practice steering left and right while moving.
Course.instructions: Accelerate with W, then use A and D to steer through the marked gates in order.
Course.hint: Steering only responds while the forklift is moving.

checkpoints.label: Slalom Gate 1
checkpoints.completeMessage: Slalom Gate 1 clear - keep weaving through the cones.

checkpoints.label: Slalom Gate 2
checkpoints.completeMessage: Slalom Gate 2 clear - keep weaving through the cones.

checkpoints.label: Slalom Gate 3
checkpoints.completeMessage: Slalom Gate 3 clear - keep weaving through the cones.

checkpoints.label: Slalom Gate 4
checkpoints.completeMessage: Slalom Gate 4 clear - keep weaving through the cones.

checkpoints.label: Slalom Gate 5
checkpoints.completeMessage: Slalom Gate 5 clear - keep weaving through the cones.

checkpoints.label: Slalom Gate 6
checkpoints.completeMessage: Slalom Gate 6 clear - keep weaving through the cones.

checkpoints.label: Slalom Gate 7
checkpoints.completeMessage: Slalom Gate 7 clear - keep weaving through the cones.

checkpoints.label: Finish Line
checkpoints.completeMessage: Serpentine complete - smooth, controlled weaving keeps loads and pedestrians safe.

Course.title: Driving Course
Course.objective: Combine starting, accelerating, braking, and steering through a full course with turns, cone lanes, and a mid-course stop.
Course.instructions: Start the engine, then drive through each checkpoint in order - weaving through the cone lanes, stopping fully at the yield point, and clearing the boundary walls - before parking in the final bay.
Course.hint: Hitting a cone or wall fails the attempt just like in Turning Practice - take the turns slowly and keep clear of the lane markers.

checkpoints.label: Checkpoint 1
checkpoints.completeMessage: Checkpoint 1 clear - a right turn is coming up.

checkpoints.label: Checkpoint 3 - Left Turn
checkpoints.completeMessage: Checkpoint 3 clear - a yield point is ahead, straighten up and be ready to stop.

checkpoints.label: Yield Point
checkpoints.completeMessage: Yield point clear - one more right turn before the parking bay.

checkpoints.label: Checkpoint 4 - Right Turn
checkpoints.completeMessage: Checkpoint 4 clear - bring the forklift to the parking bay.

checkpoints.label: Parking Bay
checkpoints.completeMessage: You completed the full driving course and parked safely.

Course.title: Pallet Pickup & Placement
Course.objective: Pick up a pallet with the forks and place it in the marked drop zone.
Course.instructions: Drive up to the pallet with the forks lowered (F), slide them under the load, raise with R to lift, carry the pallet to the drop zone, lower with F, then reverse away to release it.
Course.hint: Approach the pallet slowly and squarely - the forks only engage when they are low and centered under the load.

Course.title: Completion Summary
Course.objective: Review completed driving control tasks.
Course.instructions: Confirm engine start, acceleration, braking, turning, the driving course, and the pallet pickup task are complete.
Course.hint: Completion means you can identify and use the basic forklift operating controls in this simplified simulation.

Course.title: Scenario Briefing
Course.objective: Understand rated capacity, load stability, and the fail conditions in this assessment.
Course.instructions: Review why overloading tips a forklift forward, why cones must never be struck, and why sudden braking throws the load off the forks. Any of these fails the attempt.
Course.hint: The counterweight only balances loads up to the rated capacity shown in the HUD.

content.body:
A forklift stays upright because the counterweight balances the load - lifting more than the rated capacity shifts the combined center of gravity past the front axle and tips the truck forward.

Traffic cones mark pedestrian lanes and hazards. Striking one in this assessment fails the attempt, the same way it would fail a practical evaluation.

Sudden braking throws the load forward off the forks. Slow down early and brake gently while carrying.
content.sceneBody:
### Fail Conditions

- **Overload tip-over** - lifting a pallet heavier than the rated capacity shifts the center of gravity past the front axle and pitches the forklift forward.
- **Cone strike** - touching any traffic cone ends the attempt, the same as striking a pedestrian lane marker in a practical evaluation.
- **Load thrown off** - braking hard above walking speed throws the pallet off the forks. Slow down early and brake gently while carrying.

Rated capacity in this assessment: **1,000 kg**. After a fail, use **Reset Attempt** and try again - failed attempts are counted but never block completion.
objectives: Compare load weight against rated capacity before lifting.
Recognize that overloading tips the forklift forward.
Keep a safe path and avoid striking obstacles while carrying a load.
Brake gradually so the load does not slide off the forks.

Course.title: Precision Carry
Course.objective: Carry a pallet through a cone-lined lane and deliver it without a single fail condition.
Course.instructions: Pick up the pallet, carry it down the cone corridor to the drop zone, lower it with F, and reverse away. Hitting a cone or braking hard while carrying fails the attempt - use Reset Attempt and try again.
Course.hint: Ease off W early and let the forklift coast instead of slamming S at speed.

Course.title: Load Limits
Course.objective: Judge which pallet is within the rated capacity and deliver it safely.
Course.instructions: Three pallets are labeled with their weight. The forklift capacity is shown in the HUD. Lift a pallet within capacity and deliver it to the drop zone. Lifting the overweight pallet will tip the forklift and fail the attempt.
Course.hint: Read the weight labels before driving in - the heaviest pallet exceeds the rated capacity.

Course.title: Completion Summary
Course.objective: Review the assessment results.
Course.instructions: Confirm the precision carry and load limit exercises are complete.
Course.hint: Completion means you can plan a safe carry and refuse an overweight load.

content.completeMessage: All requirements are complete. Submit the module to record completion feedback.

Course.title: Scenario Briefing
Course.objective: Understand why shutdown and secure parking are part of safe operation.
Course.instructions: Review the expected order for parking and securing the forklift.
Course.hint: A parked forklift can still create hazards if not secured.

content.body:
Post-operation discipline prevents parked forklifts from becoming hazards.

A proficient park means the truck sits straight inside the painted lines, stopped, with forks lowered and the engine off - cones along the route mark limits that must not be touched.

Forks should be lowered, controls set to neutral, and the parking brake engaged before leaving the equipment.

Any unsafe condition or visible damage should be reported for qualified follow-up.
content.sceneBody:
### Secure Parking Discipline

- Park inside the painted bay, clear of traffic lanes and cones.
- Lower the forks flat, set controls to neutral, and engage the parking brake.
- Switch off the equipment and report anything unsafe found during the shift.

The next step is a driving exercise: the parking is only accepted when the forklift is inside the lines, straight, stopped, forks lowered, and the engine is off. Cones along the route are live - hitting one fails the attempt.
objectives: Park inside painted bay lines without striking cones or markers.
Sequence safe parking and shutdown actions.
Identify why forks, controls, and parking brake must be secured.
Recognize when unsafe conditions should be reported after operation.

Course.title: Secure Parking
Course.objective: Park the forklift inside the painted bay without striking a cone.
Course.instructions: Drive the cone-lined route to the painted parking bay, straighten up between the lines, stop completely, lower the forks with F, then switch the engine off with E. Hitting a cone fails the attempt.
Course.hint: The status badge at the top tells you which parking requirement is still missing.

Course.title: Parallel Parking
Course.objective: Ease sideways into a narrow parallel bay between the boundary cones.
Course.instructions: Steer into the gap in the left-hand cone line, straighten up so the forklift sits flush with the bay, then stop, lower the forks with F, and switch off with E.
Course.hint: The bay is only slightly wider than the forklift - small steering corrections beat big ones.

Course.title: Parking Between Forklifts
Course.objective: Park in a tight gap between two parked forklifts without clipping either one.
Course.instructions: Approach slowly and centered - the parked forklifts on both sides are live obstacles, so drifting toward either one ends the attempt just like hitting a wall.
Course.hint: Center up early. There is very little room to correct once you are between the two forklifts.

Course.title: Shutdown Sequence
Course.objective: Place post-operation steps in a safe order.
Course.instructions: Select the six shutdown actions in the correct order: park level, lower forks, neutral controls, parking brake, power off, then report concerns. Wrong picks are counted.
Course.hint: Lowering forks and securing movement controls are essential before leaving equipment.

actions.label: Park on a level surface
actions.detail: Away from traffic lanes, slopes, exits, and obstructions.

actions.label: Lower the forks completely
actions.detail: Flat on the floor so they are not a trip or impact hazard.

actions.label: Set controls to neutral
actions.detail: Direction and hydraulic levers centered before leaving the seat.

actions.label: Engage the parking brake
actions.detail: The truck must not be able to roll once you step off.

actions.label: Turn off the equipment
actions.detail: Switch the ignition off and remove the key if required.

actions.label: Report unsafe conditions or damage
actions.detail: Tell qualified personnel about anything found during the shift.

Course.title: Unsafe Condition Reporting
Course.objective: Decide what needs to be reported after operation.
Course.instructions: For each end-of-shift condition, choose Report or No Action. Correct every card to complete the step.
Course.hint: Maintenance is outside this prototype; learners should report concerns to qualified personnel.

prompts.text: A fresh oil patch is forming on the floor under the parked forklift.
prompts.feedback: Correct - fluid leaks must be reported before the next shift uses the truck.
prompts.wrongFeedback: A forming oil patch means an active leak. This must be reported.

prompts.text: The forks are lowered flat on the floor inside the parking bay.
prompts.feedback: Correct - lowered forks are the expected parked condition, nothing to report.
prompts.wrongFeedback: Lowered forks are exactly what secure parking requires - no report needed.

prompts.text: One lift chain has a kinked, stiff link after the shift.
prompts.feedback: Correct - damaged lifting parts must be reported so the truck is not used.
prompts.wrongFeedback: A kinked chain link can fail under load. This must be reported.

prompts.text: The seat belt webbing is frayed near the buckle.
prompts.feedback: Correct - a damaged seat belt is a safety device defect and must be reported.
prompts.wrongFeedback: A frayed seat belt may not restrain the operator. This must be reported.

prompts.text: The warning beacon lens is clean and flashes normally during the test.
prompts.feedback: Correct - a working beacon is a normal condition, nothing to report.
prompts.wrongFeedback: The beacon is working as designed - no report is needed.

Course.title: Scenario Briefing
Course.objective: Understand the purpose of a forklift walk-around check before operation.
Course.instructions: Review why a forklift-specific inspection separates engine-off visual checks from engine-on control checks.
Course.hint: Think of this as a safety gate before the forklift enters the work area.

content.body:
Forklift walk-around inspection adapts familiar vehicle inspection routines into equipment-specific safety checks.

Engine-off checks cover forks, mast, lift chains, hydraulic hoses, tires and wheels, counterweight, LPG tank and battery, seat belt, overhead guard, and ground leaks.

Engine-on checks confirm dashboard indicators, steering, brakes, lift and tilt functions, forward/reverse travel, horn, lights, beacon, and backup alarm before entering the work area.

syllabus.element: Element 1: Perform visual check of equipment

objectives: Differentiate engine-off and engine-on inspection tasks.
Recognize visible defects that make a forklift unsafe to use.
Practice reporting unsafe conditions before operation.

Course.title: Engine-Off Inspection
Course.objective: Inspect visible components before starting or moving the equipment.
Course.instructions: Use hotspots or inspection cards to check forks, mast, lift chains, hydraulic hoses, tires and wheels, counterweight, LPG tank and battery, seat belt, overhead guard, and ground leaks. Start the engine once every area is clear.
Course.hint: Visible leaks, unsafe tires, or damaged lifting parts should stop operation. The engine is only started after the walk-around is complete.

checks.found: Forks show no visible cracks, bending, or wear in this inspection state.
checks.label: Forks
checks.inspect: Check fork tips, heel area, and mounting pins for cracks, bending, or wear.
checks.feedback: Damaged or bent forks can fail under load and must be reported before use.

checks.found: No mast crack or damage is visible in this inspection state.
checks.label: Mast Assembly
checks.inspect: Inspect the mast channels and lift path for cracks, bending, or obstruction.
checks.feedback: A cracked or damaged mast can make lifting unsafe and must be reported.

checks.found: Lift chains appear properly lubricated with no visible damage.
checks.label: Lift Chains
checks.inspect: Check the lift chains for proper lubrication and any broken, stretched, or damaged links.
checks.feedback: Damaged, dry, or stretched chains must be reported before lifting operations.

checks.found: No hydraulic leak is visible in this inspection state.
checks.label: Hydraulic Hoses
checks.inspect: Check hydraulic hoses and cylinders for visible leaks, cracks, or wear.
checks.feedback: Hydraulic leaks can affect lifting safety and must be reported before operation.

checks.found: Tires and wheel nuts appear acceptable in this inspection state.
checks.label: Tires and Wheels
checks.inspect: Check tire condition, wheel nuts, and tire pressure (for pneumatic tires).
checks.feedback: Unsafe tire condition or loose wheel nuts affect steering and stability.

checks.found: Counterweight mounting appears secure in this inspection state.
checks.label: Counterweight
checks.inspect: Check the counterweight mounting and rear clearance for visible damage.
checks.feedback: A loose or damaged counterweight affects forklift balance and must be reported.

checks.found: No LPG leak, damaged mounting, or battery concern is visible in this inspection state.
checks.label: LPG Tank and Battery
checks.inspect: Check the propane tank, mounting bracket, hose fittings, and battery area for leaks, damage, or corrosion.
checks.feedback: A propane leak or unsafe battery condition is hazardous and must be reported before operation.
checks.targetArea: LPG tank, mounting bracket, and battery area

checks.found: Seat and seat belt appear in working condition in this inspection state.
checks.label: Seat Belt
checks.inspect: Check the seat condition and confirm the seat belt latches and retracts properly.
checks.feedback: A damaged or non-functioning seat belt must be reported before operation.

checks.found: The overhead guard shows no visible structural damage in this inspection state.
checks.label: Overhead Guard
checks.inspect: Check the overhead guard for bending, cracks, or missing sections.
checks.feedback: A damaged overhead guard reduces operator protection and must be reported.

checks.found: No fluid leak is visible on the ground in this inspection state.
checks.label: Ground Leaks
checks.inspect: Check the ground beneath the forklift for oil, fuel, hydraulic fluid, or coolant leaks.
checks.feedback: Any fluid leak on the ground must be reported before operation.

Course.title: Engine-On Inspection
Course.objective: Judge gauge readings and confirm controls respond before entering the work area.
Course.instructions: Read each dashboard gauge and decide whether it is normal or abnormal, then test the horn, lights, beacon, backup alarm, steering, brakes, lift and tilt, and travel controls.
Course.hint: Not every gauge reads normal. A warning light that stays lit or a needle in the red zone must be reported.

gauges.label: Warning Lights
gauges.correctFeedback: Correct. No warning light is lit, so the forklift is clear to continue the check.
gauges.incorrectFeedback: A dashboard with no active warning light is a normal reading.

gauges.label: Battery Charge Indicator
gauges.correctFeedback: Correct. A charge light that stays on means the charging system is not keeping up. Report it.
gauges.incorrectFeedback: A charge warning that stays lit is abnormal. It means the battery is not charging.

gauges.label: LPG Level Gauge
gauges.correctFeedback: Correct. There is enough LPG to complete the shift.
gauges.incorrectFeedback: A sufficient LPG level is a normal reading. Only a near-empty tank needs action.

gauges.label: Hour Meter
gauges.correctFeedback: Correct. The hour meter is a record, not a fault indicator. Log it and continue.
gauges.incorrectFeedback: The hour meter only records running hours. Logging the reading is a normal step.

gauges.label: Engine Temperature Gauge
gauges.correctFeedback: Correct. An overheating engine must be shut down and reported before operation.
gauges.incorrectFeedback: A needle in the red zone means overheating. That is an abnormal reading and must be reported.

devices.label: Test Horn
devices.feedback: Horn responds. Audible warning device is working in this scenario.

devices.label: Test Headlights
devices.feedback: Headlights respond. Lighting check passes in this scenario.

devices.label: Test Tail Lights
devices.feedback: Tail lights respond. Lighting check passes in this scenario.

devices.label: Test Turn Signals
devices.feedback: Turn signals respond. Signal check passes in this scenario.

devices.label: Test Warning Beacon
devices.feedback: Warning beacon responds. Visual warning check passes in this scenario.

devices.label: Test Backup Alarm
devices.feedback: Backup alarm responds. Reverse warning check passes in this scenario.

devices.label: Steering Response
devices.feedback: Steering responds smoothly with no excessive play in this training scenario.

devices.label: Brakes
devices.feedback: Service brake and parking brake respond correctly in this training scenario.

devices.label: Lift and Tilt Functions
devices.feedback: Mast raises, lowers, and tilts smoothly with no unusual noise in this training scenario.

devices.label: Forward/Reverse Travel
devices.feedback: Forward/reverse selector and accelerator respond correctly in this training scenario.

Course.title: Defect Recognition Test
Course.objective: Decide if the forklift is usable based on visible scenario conditions.
Course.instructions: Review each visual state and choose whether the forklift may be used for operation.
Course.hint: If a visible condition affects stability, steering, lifting, or fluid safety, choose No.

scenarios.title: Scenario 1: Obvious defect - leaking oil
scenarios.feedback: Visible fluid leaks may indicate engine oil, hydraulic oil, coolant, or battery electrolyte problems. The forklift should not be used until the issue is reported and cleared.
scenarios.question: Is this forklift usable for operation?

scenarios.title: Scenario 2: Good forklift
scenarios.feedback: If the walk-around inspection and engine-on controls show no unsafe condition, the forklift may proceed to supervised training use.
scenarios.question: Is this forklift usable for operation?

scenarios.title: Scenario 3: Worn-out or flat tire
scenarios.feedback: Unsafe tire condition affects steering and stability. The forklift must not be used until the issue is reported and corrected.
scenarios.question: Is this forklift usable for operation?

Course.title: Completion Summary
Course.objective: Review completed checks and scenario score.
Course.instructions: Confirm that required engine-off checks, engine-on checks, and defect recognition questions are complete.
Course.hint: Completion means the learner can identify what to inspect and when to report unsafe conditions.

ChecklistItem.text: Check for engine oil, hydraulic oil, coolant, and battery leaks.
Inspect tires for damage, wear, or unsafe condition.
Check forks, mast, carriage, and lift chain for visible damage.
Confirm horn, lights, warning beacon, and backup alarm are working.
Check gauges and dashboard indicators before operation.
Confirm brakes, steering, and controls respond before entering the work area.
Start the engine before attempting to move.
Accelerate smoothly using the forward control.
Brake smoothly and stop within the marked zone.
Steer left and right with controlled inputs.
Complete the combined guided driving course.
Park on a level surface.
Lower forks completely.
Set controls to neutral.
Engage the parking brake.
Turn off the equipment.
Report unsafe conditions or visible damage.
Check the load weight against the rated capacity before lifting.
Refuse to lift a load that exceeds the rated capacity.
Keep the travel path clear of cones and obstacles.
Brake gradually while carrying a load.
Deliver the load to the marked drop zone and reverse away.
